advances:
The whole displaced same-orientation homothetic-triangle family in the
registered subgoal is infeasible.  The elimination allows arbitrary common
displacement, arbitrary scales in the exact strict residual strip, arbitrary
three barycentric cover thresholds, and an independently optimized endpoint
slope in every row.  The obstruction is exact: one cover threshold is below
\(1/3\), and midpoint containment then forces that row's optimized endpoint
payment above the precise amount needed to beat \(2T/9\).
author: mp_r285_displaced_homothetic_counterexample
proof:
Put \(q=1-s_1-s_2-s_3>0\).  The normalized rows
\[
\ell_i=\frac{\lambda_i-s_i}{q}
\]
satisfy \(\sum_i\ell_i=1\).  An endpoint slope \(\sigma_i\) cuts
\(\ell_i\ge-\sigma_i\) on \(A_0\) and \(\ell_i\ge\sigma_i\) on
\(A_2\).  These are exactly the two thresholds in (4), with
\(h=s_i-q\sigma_i\).  Since \(q>0\), varying \(\sigma_i\) is equivalent
to varying \(h\) over all of \(\mathbb R\).  Thus (4) retains every
independent endpoint slope in accepted fact `64760c76cadff481`.

Interchanging the two endpoint slices preserves (2), (4), and (5), so
assume \(u\ge v\).  Put
\[
k=\frac{u+v}{2}
\]
and write the barycentric coordinates of \(p\) as \(c_1,c_2,c_3\).
The midpoint triangle in (2) is \(p+k(\Delta-g)\).  The minimum of its
\(i\)-th barycentric coordinate is \(c_i-k/3\).  Hence (2) is exactly
\[
\delta_i:=c_i-\frac{k}{3}\ge0\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{6}
\]

We first calculate the endpoint infimum in (4).  On \(A_0\), the maximum
of \(\lambda_i\) is
\[
b_{0i}=c_i+\frac{2u}{3},
\]
and on \(A_2\) it is
\[
b_{2i}=c_i+\frac{2v}{3}.
\]
For \(w>0\), define
\[
\chi_w(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&x\le0,\\
x^2,&0\le x\le w,\\
w^2,&x\ge w.
\end{cases}
\tag{7}
\]
The exact similar-triangle cap formula gives
\[
|A_0\cap\{\lambda_i\ge h\}|=\chi_u(b_{0i}-h).
\tag{8}
\]
Writing \(x=b_{0i}-h\), the second endpoint cap is
\[
\chi_v(D_i-x),\qquad
D_i=b_{0i}+b_{2i}-2s_i
   =2(k+\delta_i-s_i).
\tag{9}
\]
For \(u\ge v\), direct minimization of the two clipped quadratics gives
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}
\bigl(\chi_u(x)+\chi_v(D-x)\bigr)
=
\begin{cases}
0,&D\le0,\\
D^2/2,&0<D\le\sqrt2\,v,\\
v^2,&D\ge\sqrt2\,v.
\end{cases}
\tag{10}
\]
Indeed, for \(0<D\le\sqrt2v\), the choice \(x=D/2\) is unsaturated
for both caps and attains \(D^2/2\); the inequality
\(x^2+(D-x)^2\ge D^2/2\), together with the clipped endpoint cases,
proves the lower bound.  For \(D\ge\sqrt2v\), the choice \(x=0\)
makes the first cap empty and the second cap full.  Any other choice either
saturates a cap, costing at least \(v^2\), or has two active quadratic
terms, whose sum is at least \(D^2/2\ge v^2\).  The case \(D\le0\)
allows both caps to be empty.  Thus (9)-(10) prove the exact formula
\[
E_i:=
\inf_h\left(
 |A_0\cap\{\lambda_i\ge h\}|
+ |A_2\cap\{\lambda_i\ge2s_i-h\}|
\right)
=\min\left\{v^2,\,
2(k+\delta_i-s_i)_+^2\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]

We now use only the two strict area-triangle consequences of the residual
strip.  With
\[
R=\frac{v^2}{u^2},\qquad S=\frac1{u^2},
\]
the lower strip boundary satisfies \(L_0(R)\ge1-R\), while the upper
boundary satisfies \(U_0(R)\le1+R\).  Therefore
\[
S>L_0(R)\ge1-R,\qquad
S<U_0(R)\le1+R,
\]
which is equivalent to
\[
u^2<1+v^2,\qquad 1<u^2+v^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Since \(u\ge v\), the second inequality in (12) gives
\(u>1/\sqrt2\).  Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
3\left(k-\frac13\right)-\sqrt2\,v
&=\frac{3u+(3-2\sqrt2)v-2}{2}\\
&>\frac{3/\sqrt2-2}{2}>0,
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
where \(3-2\sqrt2=(\sqrt2-1)^2>0\) and \(9>8\).  Thus
\[
k-\frac13>\frac{\sqrt2\,v}{3}.
\tag{14}
\]

By (3), some \(j\) satisfies \(s_j<1/3\).  Equations (6) and (14) give
\[
k+\delta_j-s_j
>k-\frac13
>\frac{\sqrt2\,v}{3}.
\]
Both entries in the minimum in (11) are therefore strictly larger than
\(4v^2/9\), so
\[
E_j>\frac{4v^2}{9}.
\tag{15}
\]
The middle corner cap in the same row has area \(1\) if \(s_j\le0\), and
area \((1-s_j)^2\) if \(0<s_j<1/3\).  In either case,
\[
|\Delta\cap\{\lambda_j\ge s_j\}|>\frac49.
\tag{16}
\]
Combining (15)-(16) with the first strict inequality in (12) yields
\[
M_j>
\frac{4(1+v^2)}9
>
\frac{2(1+u^2+v^2)}9.
\]
This is (5).

For the near-miss `82c768ad30501452`, the low thresholds
\(s_2=s_3=3311/10000<1/3\) are exactly the rows selected above.
Their endpoint infimum is \(v^2\), which explains why the independent
midpoint-mixture proxy is strict-low while the actual optimized endpoint
rows are not.
statement:
Normalize \(|\Delta|=1\), let \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\) be the
barycentric coordinates of \(\Delta\), and let \(g\) be its centroid.  Put
\[
A_1=\Delta,\qquad
A_0=p+u(\Delta-g),\qquad
A_2=p+v(\Delta-g),
\tag{1}
\]
where \(u,v>0\), and assume
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq\Delta.
\tag{2}
\]
Assume also that the area triple
\[
(|A_0|,|A_1|,|A_2|)=(u^2,1,v^2)
\]
lies in the exact strict residual strip of accepted fact
`64760c76cadff481`.  For arbitrary real thresholds satisfying
\[
s_1+s_2+s_3<1,
\tag{3}
\]
define the exact independently optimized row masses
\[
\begin{aligned}
M_i={}&|\Delta\cap\{\lambda_i\ge s_i\}|\\
&+\inf_{h\in\mathbb R}\left(
 |A_0\cap\{\lambda_i\ge h\}|
+ |A_2\cap\{\lambda_i\ge 2s_i-h\}|
\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
\max_i M_i>\frac{2(1+u^2+v^2)}9.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently no rational or real member of the declared displaced
homothetic family is a strict three-row counterexample.
